The look of a folder of RTF reports, as numbers

Source: R/ai_style.R
tfl_rtf_style_scan.Rd

Reads every .rtf file of a folder (and its subfolders) and returns, one row a table row, what its look is made of – never its text: the cells' widths (\cellx), each cell's top and bottom border (\clbrdrt, \clbrdrb), the font size (\fs), the cells' alignment (\ql, \qc, \qr), and the file's fonts (its font table). Rows in a run, with nothing but row definitions between them, are one table.

Usage

tfl_rtf_style_scan(rtf_dir)

Arguments

rtf_dir

The folder of RTF files.

Value

A data frame: file (its name), table (its place in the file), row (in the table), n_cells, width_twips (the row's width), rel_widths (each cell's width as parts of the narrowest, | between them), border_top, border_bottom (one character a cell: 1 a border, 0 none), font_size_pt, align (one character a cell: l, c, r), fonts (the file's font table, | between).

See also

tfl_ai_style_prompt()
